description: Recommended water temperature ranges for all pool and spa types, plus effects of temperature on pool chemistry.

records.notes: Most swimmers prefer 78–82°F. Higher temperatures increase chlorine demand.
Maximum 104°F per CPSC/PHTA safety standards. Hyperthermia risk above 104°F. Children and pregnant women: lower temperatures.
Competition pools: 77–79°F per FINA guidelines. Public recreational pools: 82–84°F typical.
Dual-purpose swim spas may have separate temperature zones.

effects.description: Chlorine demand approximately doubles for every 10°C (18°F) temperature increase.
Higher temperatures increase LSI, shifting toward scale-forming. Monitor calcium and alkalinity in heated pools.
Algae growth rate increases significantly above 85°F (29°C).
CO2 off-gasses more rapidly at higher temperatures, causing pH to rise.
Without CYA, UV + heat degrade chlorine faster in warm, sunny conditions.
Salt cell output decreases significantly below 60°F (15°C). Below 50°F, most cells shut off automatically.
